title: Smooth spherical cluster models fall at least 900 times below the tested local curvature of J1646-4545
abstract: We test whether gravity from Westerlund 1 can explain the published second spin-frequency derivative of J1646-4545. For a static spherical cluster with density that does not increase with radius, we prove a line-of-sight jerk ceiling of 2GMv/R^3. At distance at least 2 kpc, mass at most one million solar masses and relative speed at most 1000 km/s, the frequency-curvature ceiling is 1.666e-27 Hz/s^2. The measured coefficient minus three formal errors is 900 times larger. Independent Gaia and binary distance estimates support a larger distance. We check the input against ATNF 2.9.0. This excludes the tested smooth-gravity explanation only if the fitted coefficient represents a local derivative. No arrival times, later timing solution, instrument test, or noise fit is available. Local encounters, companions, propagation and torque changes remain open. We supply the proof, code, aggregate results, source hashes and a retrieval script. No new signal is claimed.

display.caption: The smooth cluster ceiling remains below the published local-curvature range throughout the tested distance interval. The shaded band uses formal errors, not a noise-model confidence interval.
